# CONVEYOR

Conveyor belt that carries parts from one end to the other at a set speed, holds a limited number, and blocks the machine before it when full.

Family: move. Python builder: `m.conveyor(...)`.

## Typical uses

Use CONVEYOR for a belt where length, speed and spacing matter. Parts take time to travel, the belt holds a limited number of them, and a blocked exit backs parts up. If the stretch is only a wait with no capacity, a [DELAY](delay.md) is simpler. For a vehicle that picks up and carries a part, use [TRANSPORT](transport.md).

## Behaviour and rules

The belt holds `floor(length / spacing)` parts, at least one. A part takes `length / speed` to cross. Consecutive parts enter at least `spacing / speed` apart, so the belt can never feed faster than that. If `length` is 0, the length is the network distance between `from_node` and `to_node`.

A full belt, or one whose entry rhythm is not met, holds back the station that feeds it. That station keeps its finished part and its resource. This is blocking after service, the same rule that [BUFFER](buffer.md) follows.

At the exit, a part leaves only when `exit_resource` (if set) is taken and any downstream belt has room. The part carries the resource on, so release it downstream, for example with a PROCESS whose action is Delay Release. With neither, the belt is a delay with a capacity.

With `accumulating` on, a blocked part stops at the end and the parts behind pack against it. With it off, the whole belt stops. Optional `stops` halt each part at a point, `diverts` send some parts out sideways on the links after the first, and `merges` let parts from another block join. The `conveyor_summary` frame reports occupancy, blocked time and transit time.

## Ports

- Inputs: any number of incoming links.
- Outputs: one outgoing link.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | float | `0.0` |  | length | `length_unit` | Belt length in layout units. 0 takes the network distance between `from_node` and `to_node`. |
| `length_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `length`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `speed` | float | `1.0` | yes | speed | `speed_unit` | Belt speed, length units per model time unit. |
| `speed_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `speed`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `spacing` | float | `1.0` | yes | length | `spacing_unit` | Belt length one entity occupies; capacity is floor(length / spacing) and the entry rhythm is spacing / speed. |
| `spacing_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit of `spacing`: "base" (the model's) or one of its quantity's units. |
| `accumulating` | bool | `True` |  |  |  | True: a blocked entity stops and the others pack behind it. False: the whole belt stops while the exit is blocked. |
| `exit_resource` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Resource an entity must take to leave the belt -- the end stop that makes accumulation happen. It carries the resource onward, so release it downstream (a PROCESS with action "Delay Release"). Empty: no end stop. Either way, a belt that feeds another belt keeps its end part until that belt has room (back-pressure). |
| `from_node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Path-network node the belt starts at (drawing, and the length when `length` is 0). |
| `to_node` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Path-network node the belt ends at. |
| `stops` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Points where each part halts on the belt: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`, between 0 and the length>, "time": <number or expression>, "resource"?: <seized for the stop>}. Parts behind pack against a stop on an accumulating belt; a non-accumulating belt stops while a part is at one. Empty: none. |
| `diverts` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Points where a part may leave the belt sideways: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "condition": <expression, read once as the part reaches it>, "time"?: <push time, number or expression>, "when_full"?: "wait" (default: the part waits there for room) or "pass" (it rides on)}. Divert k leaves by outgoing link k + 1; link 0 is the belt's end. Empty: none. |
| `merges` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Points where parts from another block join the belt: {"at": <distance from the entry, in the unit of `length`>, "from": <the block linking to this belt whose parts join there>, "priority"?: "belt" (default: they wait for a gap of two spacings) or "merge" (parts on the belt make room)}. Accumulating belts only. Empty: none. |

## Statistics

Every run fills `system` and `entity_summary` (see the [KPI reference](../kpis.md)). The example below also fills:

| Frame | Columns |
|---|---|
| `conveyor_summary` | `Run`, `Conveyor`, `Length`, `Capacity`, `Entered`, `Exited`, `Avg Occupancy`, `Max Occupancy`, `Blocked %`, `Avg Transit Time` |
| `material_flow_summary` | `Run`, `From`, `To`, `Entities` |

## Problem codes

A check of the model reports these about this block:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_CONVEYOR_DIVERT` | A CONVEYOR divert is not {at, condition, time?, when_full?}, its `at` is off the belt or on another point, its condition is empty, its time is not a number >= 0 or an expression, its when_full is not wait/pass, the belt has fewer links than 1 + diverts, or a "pass" divert's link does not go straight to a CONVEYOR, BUFFER or queue_capacity station. |
| `E_CONVEYOR_MERGE` | A CONVEYOR merge is not {at, from, priority?}, its `at` is off the belt or on another point, its `from` is not a block linking to the belt or is named twice, its priority is not belt/merge, or the belt is not accumulating. |
| `E_CONVEYOR_PARAM` | A CONVEYOR's length, speed or spacing is not a number > 0, or its endpoints name unknown nodes. |
| `E_CONVEYOR_STOP` | A CONVEYOR stop is not {at, time, resource?}, its `at` is not between 0 and the belt's length, its time is not a number >= 0 or an expression, or its resource is not declared. |
| `E_INITIAL_BELT` | A part on a belt in initial_state does not fit the model: not one entity at an accumulating CONVEYOR, a stage it does not have, a time on the wrong side of the clock, or more than one part at the belt's end. |
| `W_CONVEYOR_STOP_HELD` | A CONVEYOR stop seizes a resource a part still holds when it gets there (seized upstream, not yet released); the run stops with an error when a part asks for it twice. |

## Example

The snippet seeds itself; its output is from a run made when this page was generated.

```python
from nagasim import build as nb

m = nb.Model(time_limit=300, time_unit="seconds")
m.create(distribution=nb.Constant(value=5)) >> m.conveyor(length=30, speed=1.0, spacing=1.0) >> m.dispose()

results = m.run(seed=1)
print(results["conveyor_summary"].round(2).to_string(index=False))
```

```text
 Run   Conveyor  Length  Capacity  Entered  Exited  Avg Occupancy  Max Occupancy  Blocked %  Avg Transit Time
   1 conveyor_1    30.0        30       61      55           5.75            6.0        0.0              30.0
```
